title: Real Account
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Orphaned high schooler Ataru Kashiwagi lives in poverty with his younger sister Yuri and finds refuge in friends on the social network Real Account. He and about 10,000 users are pulled into a virtual version of the app, where the mascot Marble forces them into deadly games: a player who loses all followers dies, and when a player dies, so do their followers, while the world watches. Ataru teams up with his look-alike Yuuma to survive and find the masterminds; the series ends with the site destroyed and its creators dead (Wikipedia; ANN review).
life_message: Online popularity is a hollow measure of friendship; real bonds, especially family, are worth protecting.

content.note: Death games with mass deaths; gore across the run though the first volume's tension is mostly psychological (Wikipedia; ANN review; AniList Gore, Death Game; MU Massacre, Play or Die Situation).
Life-or-death stakes for players and followers watching worldwide (Wikipedia; ANN review; MU Survival Game).
Nudity and ecchi elements tagged (AniList Nudity, Ecchi genre; MangaDex suggestive); not mentioned in the review or Wikipedia, so capped (to verify).
A background sign reading an f-word parody (ANN review); other profanity unverified.
Ending news report of two bullied teenagers' suicides; grief and poverty after parents' deaths (Wikipedia; MU Bullying, Dead Parent/s).
Manipulative, dishonest tactics to survive (MU Manipulative Protagonist, Dishonest Protagonist).
Satire of social media follower culture (ANN review; AniList Satire).

dominant: Social-media satire; survival game; family loyalty

frames.concerns: Spectacle of mass death and gore; fan service.

frames.aligns: Vanity of the follower count exposed.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Survival by wits and tactics more than personal honor.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Imposed game rules contrasted with players' bids to escape them.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Ataru's first priority is protecting his sister Yuri.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Follower counts create a hierarchy the story mocks.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival dominates; online self-expression is the trap.

folkways.japan: Concern about netto culture, bullying and youth isolation in Japan shapes the satire.

delivery.evidence: ANN review of volume 1 calls its social-media message heavy-handed and unsubtle; Wikipedia ending stresses the internet's dark side.
delivery.note: The ending grants the internet some potential for good through Yuuma, softening an otherwise one-sided critique.

winners_losers: Ataru survives and the creators die; online popularity loses. The dark side of the internet persists in the ending.
